title: Epigenomic signatures reveal mechanistic clues and predictive markers for autism spectrum disorder.
one_liner_zh: 该文综述自闭症的表观基因组学（DNA甲基化）特征及其预测标志物，虽提及转录因子结合，但核心是表观遗传与临床预测，无蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) comprises a heterogeneous group of neurodevelopmental outcomes in children with a commonality in deficits in social communication and language combined with repetitive behaviors and interests. The etiology of ASD is heterogeneous, as several hundred genes have been implicated as well as multiple in utero environmental exposures. Over the past two decades, epigenetic investigations, including DNA methylation, have emerged as a novel way to capture the complex interface of multivariate ASD etiologies. More recently, epigenome-wide association studies using human brain and surrogate accessible tissues have revealed some convergent genes that are epigenetically altered in ASD, many of which overlap with known genetic risk factors. Unlike transcriptomes, epigenomic signatures defined by DNA methylation from surrogate tissues such as placenta and cord blood can reflect past differences in fetal brain gene transcription, transcription factor binding, and chromatin. For example, the discovery of NHIP (neuronal hypoxia inducible, placenta associated) through an epigenome-wide association in placenta, identified a common genetic risk for ASD that was modified by prenatal vitamin use. While epigenomic signatures are distinct between different genetic syndromic causes of ASD, bivalent chromatin and some convergent gene pathways are consistently epigenetically altered in both syndromic and idiopathic ASD, as well as some environmental exposures. Together, these epigenomic signatures hold promising clues towards improved early prediction and prevention of ASD as well genes and gene pathways to target for pharmacological interventions. Future advancements in single cell and multi-omic technologies, machine learning, as well as non-invasive screening of epigenomic signatures during pregnancy or newborn periods are expected to continue to impact the translatability of the recent discoveries in epigenomics to precision public health.
abstract_zh: 自闭症谱系障碍（ASD）包含一组异质性的神经发育结果，其共同特征在于社交沟通和语言缺陷，并伴有重复行为和兴趣。ASD的病因具有异质性，已涉及数百个基因以及多种宫内环境暴露。在过去二十年中，包括DNA甲基化在内的表观遗传学研究，已成为捕捉ASD多因素病因复杂交互作用的新途径。近期，利用人脑和替代可及组织进行的表观基因组关联研究，揭示了一些在ASD中表观遗传改变的趋同基因，其中许多与已知的遗传风险因素重叠。与转录组不同，来自替代组织（如胎盘和脐带血）的DNA甲基化定义的表观基因组特征，能够反映胎儿脑基因转录、转录因子结合及染色质状态的过往差异。例如，通过胎盘中表观基因组关联研究发现的NHIP（神经元缺氧诱导、胎盘相关）基因，识别出ASD的常见遗传风险，该风险受产前维生素使用调节。尽管不同遗传综合征型ASD的表观基因组特征各异，但在综合征型和特发性ASD以及某些环境暴露中，二价染色质和某些趋同基因通路始终发生表观遗传改变。总体而言，这些表观基因组特征为改善ASD的早期预测和预防，以及为药物干预靶向的基因和基因通路提供了有希望的线索。未来在单细胞和多组学技术、机器学习以及孕期或新生儿期非侵入性表观基因组特征筛查方面的进展，预计将持续推动表观基因组学最新发现向精准公共卫生的转化。
